title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: exclude specific domains from web grounding
summary: Hold: Microsoft now documents a preview API that can configure tenant-level web search, contrary to the table's claim that automation is undocumented. The Purview command creates a policy but does not configure the web-search blocking action, so it is not an automation equivalent for that control. The exclusion script, limits, default and roadmap details are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap feature lets administrators specify sites to exclude from web grounding in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: This feature will allow admins to specify a limited set of sites to exclude from web grounding in M365 Copilot and Copilot Chat #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: When web search is enabled, Copilot and Copilot Chat may ground responses in public web content.
claims.quote: When web search is enabled, Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat may fetch information from the Bing search service when information from the web helps to provide a better, more grounded response.

claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot is a Cloud Policy control governing web search in both Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: The primary way that IT admins can control access to web search is by using the Allow web search in Copilot policy, which is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365. This policy applies to both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The web-search policy can be configured for the tenant or for groups.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.claim: The policy can enable web search in Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: The policy can disable web search in Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: The policy can disable web search in work mode while leaving web mode and Copilot Chat enabled.
claims.quote: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path is Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration. You can search for the policy by name
claims.fix: The printed steps are correct but stop on the policy-selection page. Extend the path to 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. The setting name is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for configuring the web-search policy.
claims.quote: Controls web search availability in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch", "resourceVersion": 1, "properties": { "value": "0" }
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api null with kind 'graph', call 'POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta'. Add to the note: 'Preview, tenant-level automation only; fails if the setting exists in a group-level Cloud Policy. Set mode to applyOnce and include baseline.resources with resourceType microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch, resourceVersion 1, and properties.value as the string 0 (enabled), 1 (disabled), or 2 (work mode disabled). Requires delegated access and the signed-in user's AI Administrator role.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources for the resource and restrictions. The existing UI still supports group scope.

claims.claim: Purview DLP can block external web search when prompt text matches configured sensitive information types.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: The Purview path is Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.

claims.claim: The DLP rule uses Content contains > Sensitive information types.
claims.quote: Add a rule with the Content contains > Sensitive information types condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.

claims.claim: The DLP action is Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.
claims.quote: In the same rule, set the action to Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.

claims.claim: The documented procedure saves and turns on the DLP policy.
claims.quote: Save and turn on the policy.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <name> -Locations <location> -EnforcementPlanes @('CopilotExperiences') is the automation equivalent for blocking sensitive content in web search.
claims.quote: The fourth command creates the DLP policy using the $loc variable for the value of the Locations parameter ... The last command creates the DLP rule
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api to null and remove the policy-creation command from the rendered table and its explanatory prose. Replace the automation note with 'The policy-creation cmdlet does not set Performing Web Searches; an automation call for that action is not yet documented.' The command and its parameters exist, but creating the policy does not configure the blocking rule. Targeted searches and the New-DlpComplianceRule and Set-DlpComplianceRule references returned no Copilot web-search action syntax.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy creates the policy only, and a separate rule is needed.
claims.quote: Use the New-DlpCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create data loss prevention (DLP) policies ... DLP policies contain DLP rules that identify, monitor, and protect sensitive information.

claims.claim: The feature's licensing model is unknown because no feature-specific licence is published.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat (Basic) is the standalone baseline experience included with eligible Microsoft 365 licenses. You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the notes with 'Copilot Chat (Basic) is included with eligible Microsoft 365 licenses; the full Copilot experience uses the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license. Feature-specific domain-exclusion licensing is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-overview. Only product-level licensing was found; the feature-specific absence is true, but 'unknown' understates the published product entitlement.

claims.claim: Filtering incoming web results does not turn off the generated web-search queries sent to Bing.
claims.quote: When web search is enabled ... Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: Generated Bing queries consist of a few words informed by the prompt.
claims.quote: This generated search query is different from the user's original prompt-it consists of a few words informed by the user's prompt.

claims.claim: Generated queries do not include entire Microsoft 365 files.
claims.quote: The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service: ... Entire Microsoft 365 files (for example, emails or documents) or files uploaded into Copilot

claims.claim: Generated queries can be informed by organizational document content.
claims.quote: it may also be informed by data within a Microsoft 365 document ... When a user enters a prompt into Copilot inside a Microsoft 365 application ... When the user explicitly references a specific document in their prompt.

claims.claim: A manager's name obtained from Microsoft 365 data can form the Bing query.
claims.quote: Copilot finds the name of the user's manager from Microsoft 365 data. It then generates a Bing search query based on their name to see what information about them is available on the web.

claims.claim: Very short prompts can themselves be included in the generated search query.
claims.quote: The user's entire prompt, unless the prompt is very short (for example, "local weather")

claims.claim: The medium impact rating agrees with a rationale describing a configured change affecting every Copilot user.
claims.quote: impact: "medium"; impact: Medium. Changes what web sources every Copilot user may see cited once configured.
claims.fix: Set impact to 'high' and change the rationale to 'High. The tenant exclusion list changes which web page sources Copilot and Copilot Chat users may see cited once configured.' The schema defines high as most users, whereas medium is specific roles or one business unit; the verified control is tenant-wide.
